new_statements.quote: As stated above, most words are one syllable roots. If a word is multi-syllabic, simply stated, stress falls on the root. Prefixes and clitics never receive primary stress. In compounds or phrases, the stress is usually on the last syllable: gɪl:ˈgiʔd ‘sandal’, ngɪt ˈfrɪt ‘roasted chicken’ (frit ‘fried’ Sp. frito). Vowels in unstressed roots or of suffixes move to a more central vowel space, are reduced phonetically to schwa [ə], and sometimes are deleted, making identification of the vowel phoneme difficult.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are mostly monosyllabic roots; in polymorphemic words primary stress is on the root syllable, never on prefixes or clitics; in compounds and phrases the stress is usually on the final (root) syllable. Unstressed root/suffix vowels centralize to schwa or delete. The language also has two lexical tones (L, H) plus an LH contour with low functional load (§2.4, pp. 37-40), and vowel length is conditioned partly by stress placement (p. 33).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described for words; secondary stress is marked only in the elicitation frame phrase (p. 50, ex. 25: 'ˌ marks secondary stress in the phrase').
new_statements.exceptions: 'usually' on the last syllable of compounds/phrases; no lexical exceptions listed. Loanword diphthongs reduce to the vowel with primary stress (p. 42).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (root vs. affix/clitic) plus a compound/phrase-level statement; based on 'initial analysis' of elicited words and frames from six adult male speakers of San Francisco Ozolotepec.
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand stress statement found describes San Francisco Ozolotepec Zapotec (SFOZ). Ethnologue (zao entry: 'Most towns with Ozolotepec in the name included, but not San Francisco Ozolotepec'; ztg entry lists San Francisco Ozolotepec), SIL Mexico and Leander herself (pp. xiv fn.1, 1 fn.2: 'SFOZ and SCXZ... given the same ISO 639-3 code ztg') all assign SFOZ to Xanaguía Zapotec [ztg] = Glottolog xana1235, and Beam de Azcona 2019 treats it as Cisyautepecan, not Miahuatec. Glottolog nevertheless files the companion Heise 2003 sketch of the same community under ozol1235 (and its 2009 reprint under xana1235), so the SFOZ literature is the only 'description' Glottolog knows for zao. Ozolotepec Zapotec proper (zao: San Marcial, San Gregorio, San Juan Ozolotepec, San Mateo Piñas; the 'Ozolotepec variety of Miahuatec' per Beam de Azcona) has no located phonology, grammar or dictionary; its only open text is the 2007 La Liga Bíblica NT, which carries no orthographic or accent note. Recommend entering the Leander statement under xana1235 (currently marked SOURCE-NAMED-UNREACHABLE in the audit) and leaving ozol1235 as no-first-hand-source unless the reviewer accepts Glottolog's attribution.
